design.affected_system: urban water supply, distribution, and conservation system
alternatives: activate conservation from median storage projections
use conservative triggers tied to lower inflow bounds
coordinate source switching and demand stages across ensemble scenarios
assumptions: Supply, demand, leakage, and storage balances use reconciled units and meter coverage.
Restriction response and climate sequences are observed inputs or labeled scenarios.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
design.baseline: Existing sources, tariffs, and operating rules continue through the forecast horizon.

constraints.description: Forecast operations must preserve the adopted emergency storage and environmental-flow reserve.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

design.decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
design.decision_owner: water utility general manager and drought-response lead
design.decision_question: What seasonal probability distribution of storage and shortage follows climate, demand, and operating assumptions?

independence_key.binding_constraint: Forecast operations must preserve the adopted emergency storage and environmental-flow reserve.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Hindcasts meet inflow, demand, storage, shortage-event, and interval-coverage criteria across dry years.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: ensemble hydrologic and demand balance forecasting

design.intended_claim: A versioned forecast design for comparing declared alternatives affecting seasonal urban water supply-demand balance, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in expected potable-water shortage volume
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a climate-conditioned water balance a deterministic shortage prediction.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Hindcasts meet inflow, demand, storage, shortage-event, and interval-coverage criteria across dry years.

design.title: Forecast drought supply-demand balance
transportability_risks: Water rights, source portfolios, pricing, metering, leakage, and climate regimes differ.
Household conservation behavior may not transfer across tariff and tenure systems.

family.affected_system: urban water supply, distribution, and conservation system
claim_boundary: Hazard observations and modeled exposure do not establish individual harm or causation.
Proposed adaptations are planning alternatives, not adopted policy or engineered designs.
A design-only record is not a city execution, validated forecast, or impact result.
family.decision_owner: water utility general manager and drought-response lead
family.description: Decision designs for water loss diagnosis, demand and supply forecasting, renewal and reuse investment, distribution, scheduling, multi-year stress, and conservation evaluation.
family.title: Drought and urban water security

library_claim_boundary: The catalog contains 240 decision designs, not 240 city executions.
Exactly twelve designs map to existing Tier-D reference templates; 228 remain design-only.
A reference implementation can be an explicit negative release and does not imply impact.
No record claims a city binding, new method, deployment, adoption, or real-user outcome.
Future execution requires source binding, gate passage, and domain, legal, community, and operational review.
